info.title: AI Chat API
info.description: Backend API for the AI chat application: authentication (including SMS two-step verification), AI characters, conversations, messages, memories, and streamed AI replies (SSE). All endpoints except `/auth/register`, `/auth/login` and `/auth/login/otp` require a Bearer token.

post.description: Creates a user account. The password is hashed with Argon2id and never stored in plaintext. Usernames are unique.

post.summary: Log in and obtain an access token
post.description:
Exchanges username/password for a signed JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on protected endpoints.

When the account has two-step verification enabled, no token is issued: the response instead carries `otp_required` plus a `challenge_id`, and the login is completed with `POST /auth/login/otp`.

Second step for accounts with two-step verification: exchanges the `challenge_id` from `POST /auth/login` plus the code received by SMS for the same access token a normal login would have returned. An incorrect or expired code is rejected with 400 — never 401, which would sign the caller out of an unrelated session.

patch.description: Update the username, display name and/or the default AI model. The username must be unique — a duplicate is 409.

post.description: Sends a one-time code to the supplied mobile number. Nothing is stored and the second factor stays off until `POST /me/otp/verify` confirms the code.

post.summary: Confirm the code and enable two-step verification
post.description: Verifies the code sent by `/me/otp/enable`, stores the verified mobile number and turns two-step verification on. An invalid or expired code is rejected with 400 and leaves the account unchanged.
Turns two-step verification off for the authenticated user and discards any code still in flight. The verified mobile number is kept.
Only `name` is required. The persona belongs to the authenticated user; `user_id` is taken from the access token and never from the request body.

get.summary: Get one of the user's personas

delete.description: Conversations that used the persona are kept and fall back to no persona (USER_PERSONA_ID becomes NULL).

get.description: Built-in characters plus the ones the authenticated user created. Another user's private characters are never listed. Administrators are scoped the same way here; they reach other characters through `GET /characters/{character_id}` and the write endpoints.

post.description: Creates a character owned by the authenticated user; the owner comes from the access token, so the character is visible only to its creator. Administrators may also pass `owner_user_id` (explicit `null` creates a global character) and `status`; for anyone else those fields are rejected with 403.

patch.description: Owners may edit their own characters; administrators may edit any character and additionally reassign `owner_user_id` or set `status`.

delete.description: Marks the character DELETED; the row and any conversations referencing it are preserved. Owners may delete their own characters, administrators any character.

post.description: Returns the signature and parameters the browser needs to upload an image straight to Cloudinary. The image never passes through this API, and the API secret is never returned. Answers 503 when the CLOUDINARY_* settings are not configured.

get.description: Models available for conversations; used to pick a conversation's model. Administrators also see inactive models.

post.description: Administrators only. The provider and endpoint must already exist.

get.description: Active models for any user; administrators can also fetch inactive ones.

delete.summary: Delete an AI model (admin, soft delete)
delete.description: Administrators only. Sets ACTIVE=0 so conversations and telemetry that reference the model keep their foreign keys.

post.description: Starts a conversation with an AI character. The model defaults to the user's default model, then to the first active model.

get.summary: Get one of the user's conversations

delete.description: Marks the conversation DELETED; the row and its messages are preserved.

get.description: Returns messages in chronological order. Use `before_id` (exclusive) with `limit` to page backwards through history.

schema.title: Response List Messages Conversations  Conversation Id  Messages Get

post.summary: Send a message and stream the AI reply (Server-Sent Events)
post.description: Persists the user message, then streams the AI reply incrementally as SSE. Events: `message.created` (the persisted user message), repeated `message.delta` (incremental text), `message.completed` (the persisted assistant message + token usage), or `error` if the AI provider fails.

404.description: Conversation not found or not owned by the caller

get.description: Long-term memories scoped to the authenticated user, optionally filtered by character. Only active memories are returned.

system_prompt.title: System Prompt
system_prompt.description: Persona / system prompt sent to the model

owner_user_id.title: Owner User Id
owner_user_id.description: Admin only. Omit to own it yourself; null creates a global character.

CharacterCreate.title: CharacterCreate
CharacterCreate.description:
Body for POST /characters.

For a normal user the owner is always the authenticated user — never the request
body. An administrator may additionally pass ``owner_user_id`` (explicit ``null``
creates a global/built-in character) and ``status``.
Lengths mirror the ``CHARACTERS`` column widths.

owner_user_id.title: Owner User Id
owner_user_id.description: null for built-in characters; the creator for private ones

owner_user_id.title: Owner User Id
owner_user_id.description: Admin only. null makes the character global.

CharacterUpdate.title: CharacterUpdate
CharacterUpdate.description:
Body for PATCH /characters/{id} — at least one field must be provided.

Owners may edit ``name``/``description``/``avatar_url``/``system_prompt`` on their
own characters; ``owner_user_id`` and ``status`` are administrator-only.

model_id.title: Model Id
model_id.description: Defaults to the user's default model

user_persona_id.title: User Persona Id
user_persona_id.description: Optional persona the user role-plays as. Must belong to the authenticated user. Omit for no persona — the AI then just follows the character prompt.

user_persona.description: null when the conversation has no persona

LoginOtpRequest.title: LoginOtpRequest
LoginOtpRequest.description: Body for POST /auth/login/otp — the second step of a two-step login.

LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse
LoginResponse.description: Successful login: a bearer access token plus the user profile.

MessageCreate.title: MessageCreate
MessageCreate.description: Body for POST /conversations/{id}/messages (starts a streamed AI reply).

ModelRead.title: ModelRead
ModelRead.description:
A model offered for conversations.

Endpoint credentials (``AI_ENDPOINTS.BASE_URL`` / ``API_KEY``) are never exposed —
only the endpoint's id.

ModelUpdate.title: ModelUpdate
ModelUpdate.description: Body for PATCH /models/{id} (administrators only) — at least one field.

code_expires_in_seconds.title: Code Expires In Seconds
code_expires_in_seconds.description: Lifetime of the code, in seconds

mobile_hint.title: Mobile Hint
mobile_hint.description: Masked number the code was sent to

OtpChallengeRead.title: OtpChallengeRead
OtpChallengeRead.description: A code has been sent; the challenge id ties the next call to this attempt.

OtpEnableRequest.title: OtpEnableRequest
OtpEnableRequest.description:
Body for POST /me/otp/enable — the local 10-digit mobile number.

Length is only bounded to keep the payload sane; the shape is validated by
``normalize_mobile``, which explains what is wrong instead of returning a
schema error.

code_expires_in_seconds.title: Code Expires In Seconds
code_expires_in_seconds.description: Lifetime of the code, in seconds

OtpRequiredResponse.title: OtpRequiredResponse
OtpRequiredResponse.description:
The password was correct, but two-step verification is enabled.

No token is issued yet, and deliberately no hint about which number the code
went to: that would disclose the phone suffix to anyone holding the password,
which is exactly what the second factor protects against.

PersonaCreate.title: PersonaCreate
PersonaCreate.description: Body for POST /personas. The owner always comes from the access token.

PersonaUpdate.title: PersonaUpdate
PersonaUpdate.description: Body for PATCH /personas/{id} — at least one field must be provided.

folder.title: Folder
folder.description: Cloudinary folder the signed upload must target

UploadSignatureRead.title: UploadSignatureRead
UploadSignatureRead.description:
Response for POST /cloudinary/signature.

``folder`` and ``timestamp`` are echoed so the browser can send exactly the
parameters that were signed.

UserRead.title: UserRead
UserRead.description: Public user profile. Never contains the password hash.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description:
Body for PATCH /me — at least one field must be provided.

``username`` follows the same rules as registration; uniqueness is enforced
by the database and reported as 409.
